text:
anya: Quick follow-up from the fused-attn RFC review — wanted to capture open tradeoffs around fused-QKV vs fused-bias/rope and the dropout-free inference path. TL;DR: we need a clear runtime selector + model metadata flags, and tests for cache correctness.

mike: agree. main worry is cache layout when we fuse QKV + rope bias. caching currently assumes separate q/k/v tensors.

surya: can you sketch the incompatible cases? e.g., transposed layouts, quantized tensors, streamed KV append?

anya: short list: 1) fused-QKV expects contiguous 3*H last-dim layout (`[B,S,3,H]` or `[B,3,H,S]` depending), 2) rope-bias fusion wants to apply position multipliers pre-split (makes incremental caching trickier), 3) dropout ops removal only safe for inference if model wasn't trained with MC-dropout for uncertainty.

jess: on (2) — if we apply rope+bias before splitting, we have to store cached keys already-rope’d or store raw keys and reapply rope on read. both have perf vs memory tradeoffs.

mike: storing pre-rope KV reduces per-token compute but increases memory and complicates multi-model packing. we need a policy: prefer memory or prefer latency.

oliver: experimented with fused-QKV on A100: fused kernel => 6-9% throughput gain for short seqs (<512) and 2-3% for long seqs. fused-rope gave an additional ~3% in our microbench. numbers vary by head dim.

surya: nice. did you test with kv-cache streaming? 

oliver: yes — but only when we stored pre-rope K/V. If we reapply rope on every step, perf win disappears.

anya: proposal: runtime exposes `kernel_capabilities` metadata per model artifact, eg: `supports_fused_qkv`, `supports_fused_rope_bias`, `dropout_free_safe`. runtime selector picks fused kernel only if model declares capability and server config permits.

mike: +1. also add dynamic checks: if request has `force_detach_kv=true` or uses `cross-attention` layout fallback, skip fused path.

jess: we should also version the capability flags. i.e., `fused_qkv:v1` so we can change ABI later.

surya: good call. and add a small heuristic table in kernel selector: (seq_len, batch, head_dim, dtype) -> preferred kernel. fallback to reference if memory mismatch.

anya: about dropout-free: simpler — for inference we bypass dropout ops entirely. but models exported from TF/other libs sometimes embed dropout as fused patterns. need a detection pass in model loader to rewrite/remove those ops safely.

mike: loader rewrite should assert `deterministic_inference` metadata or we add a `force_dropout_removed` opt-in. can't just assume.

oliver: test plan: unit tests for numerical parity (small inputs), microbench harness for perf, and 1k-sample prompt set for regression detection (latency + token-level logits diffs). also add a canary rollout in Dedicated with 5% traffic.

jess: for parity tests include kv-cache correctness for stepped generation. most subtle bugs show up on streaming generation.

surya: implementation notes: fused-QKV kernel needs `qkv_stride` and `qkv_offset` in kernel params; rope fusion needs `rope_phase` precomputed and either stored per-cache-entry or recomputed cheaply. prefer precompute on CPU when mem budget allows.

mike: API change needed: `ModelServeConfig` add `kernel_compat_flags: ["fused_qkv:v1","fused_rope:v2"]` and `inference_safety: ["dropout_free"]`. these are strings so we can evolve.

anya: rollout plan: (1) loader + metadata, (2) implement fused kernels behind feature gates, (3) integrative parity tests, (4) canary, (5) enable by default for verified models.

oliver: minor: watch out for quantized path. fused kernels need explicit qint layout support. otherwise selector should pick dequantize->fused or native quant kernel.

jess: ops for logs + tracing: add per-request annotation `kernel_used` and `capability_mismatch` to make postmortem easier.

surya: any objections to adding a `prefer_memory_over_latency` flag for per-tenant policy? some customers prefer lower latency even if memory spike.

mike: we'll need quota enforcement if memory-heavy policies can OOM nodes. but configurable per-tenant makes sense.

anya: ok i'll draft a small follow-up doc with the proposed `ModelServeConfig` JSON schema, kernel selector heuristic table, and test checklist. will ping for reviews.

runtime-bot: deploy-check: canary pipeline status: green for fused-qkv branch on `canary/runtime` — 0 failures.

jess: sweet. thanks everyone, looking forward to the draft.

anya: thanks — will post the RFC follow-up w/ config examples in #eng-runtime next hour.
